title: st.fragment incompatible with streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit dashboards with st.fragment and the unit testing framework are not compatible. When a function is defined with st.fragment, it never runs in unit tests, so it can't be tested

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
App file

[USER].fragment()
def dummy_result():
  return "testing"
```
Unit test file
```
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest
from app import dummy_result

at = AppTest.from_file("app.py")
at.run()
result = dummy_result()
assert result == "testing"

```
```


### Steps To Reproduce

`pytest test.py`

### Expected Behavior

the test should pass

### Current Behavior

It fails because result is NoneType

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.0
- Python version: 3.11.5
- Operating System: MacOs



### Additional Information

_No response_

Still the problem occures, What is seen only status changed here.

If you enable the debugger, you will notice there some element of the UnknownElement type
In addition, the list **currently** does not have  `fragment` https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/app-testing/st.testing.v1.apptest

As far as I understand, testing support is only for important action elements. To write a good test, you need to interact with buttons and so on.

I checked this against current `develop`. Fragments do run under `AppTest`:

- During `AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()`, the fragment body runs and its return value reaches the script.
- A button inside the fragment works with `.click().run()`. `AppTest` reruns the whole script rather than only the fragment. That gives the same result unless a test depends on the rest of the script *not* rerunning.

The test in the report calls `dummy_result()` directly from the test module. A `[USER].fragment` function runs only during a Streamlit script run. Outside one, it returns `None` without running its body, so `result` is `None`. Instead, assert on what the app renders through `AppTest`. Or move the logic into a plain function and unit-test that function directly.

#17605 documents this in the bundled testing skill. `AppTest` doesn't support fragment-scoped reruns yet (rerunning only the fragment, as the browser does). That gap is tracked with dialog inner widgets in #9786, so I'm closing this one as working as intended.
